\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انطلق} (inṭalaqa)}{انطلق (inṭalaqa)}]{\ar{انطلق} (inṭalaqa) — to set off}

\label{lesson:AR-C226-intalaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to use, then the Arabic for to bring.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انطلق}}
\textbf{\ar{انطلق}} — \emph{inṭalaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to set off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انطلق}} (\emph{inṭalaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-l-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to be free, to be let go\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Inṭalaqa} is Form VII, \textquotedblleft{}to be let loose\textquotedblright{}, to set off.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inṭalaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inṭalaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{inṭalaqa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to use, then the Arabic for to bring, then say \emph{inṭalaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شحن} (shaḥana)}{شحن (shaḥana)}]{\ar{شحن} (shaḥana) — to charge (a phone); to ship}

\label{lesson:AR-C226-shahana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to bring, then the Arabic for to set off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شحن}}
\textbf{\ar{شحن}} — \emph{shaḥana} — \textquotedblleft{}to charge (a phone); to ship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شحن}} (\emph{shaḥana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-ḥ-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to load, to fill\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Shaḥana} is to load a ship; charging a battery is a modern sense.
\end{cousinweb}
